question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

Unless you don’t / work hard, / you will fail.
solution:
The correct answer is **'Unless you don't'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Conditional sentences** have two parts or clauses that give a condition in the dependent clause and a result in the independent clause.
 
• **The first conditional**__ is a structure used for talking about possibilities in the present or in the future. 
 __
 
• **E.g.**__- If I wake up early, I always read in bed.
 
 
 
• **'Unless'** means, 'if not'. So, to change 'if' to 'unless', we need to negate the rest of the subordinate clause.
 __
 
• **E.g.**__- My uncle can help us unless he doesn’t get off work soon enough.
 
 

Hence, the correct sentence would be "**Unless you work hard, you will fail."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Zero Conditional**__**: **We use the zero conditional to talk about permanent truths, such as scientific facts, and general habits.

 __
 
• **E.g.**__- If you eat a lot, you put on weight.
 
 
 
• __**The Second Conditional**__**: **We use the second conditional to talk about improbable or impossible situations in the present or future.
 __
 
• **E.g.**__- If I were rich, I’d spend all my time travelling.
 
 
 
• __**The Third Conditional**__**: **We use the third conditional to talk about impossible situations, as in the second conditional, in the past.
 
• We often use the third conditional to describe regrets.
 __
 
• **E.g.**__- If we had left earlier, we would have arrived on time.
